evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never delivered the time-boxed framing or promise of a dependable quote before diving into discovery. Jumped straight into 'I have this as a good contact number' and 'do you have any questions or concerns' without the quid pro quo setup.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Drew), moving day (Friday October 2nd), route (3100 S. Verona Crossing, Austin to 3001 per a Crossing, Austin), and size (800 sq ft apartment) all confirmed early in the call.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked 'before we go over all the details besides pricing, do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call today?' — this came very early, before logistics probing, but customer said 'not at the moment,' so no actual concerns were raised to follow up on.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised no concerns, so N/A per rubric.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns were raised, so N/A per rubric.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floor/stories (second floor, fourth floor destination), rooms (not explicitly numbered but size stated as 800 sq ft and 1000 sq ft), walking distance (50 feet from truck to origin, destination walk flagged as uncertain), special considerations (queen bed, 65-70" TV, couch, work table, coffee table, bar chairs, dresser, mattresses, nightstand, lamps), additional stops (none mentioned).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' Customer volunteered he doesn't plan to use boxes, but rep did not offer packing services as a service option.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asked 'the typical number of boxes for a move this size is about 15 to 25 boxes. Do you feel like you fall within that range?' — customer confirmed he's minimal and won't use boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave typical range for the move size ('two and a half and four hours') and personalized to this customer's specific details: 'since we're moving from the second floor, the fourth floor with elevator access just across the street... since we're moving minimal boxes and just those items that you listed... you would definitely fall within three to four hour range.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed hourly rate ($220), crew size (2 movers), truck size (26 foot box truck), included services (fuel, truck, taxes, insurance, pads, tools), and no fees/charges to cancel or change. Also mentioned '2.5 hour range' and stated 'no deposit required.' Did not explicitly frame as 'not a guess' or mention 15-minute increments, but the core transparency is there.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' after giving the estimate. Customer asked clarifying questions about the hourly rate and duration, rep answered, but the specific check was never deployed.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'we do have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you can't make it in a time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill' — covers the discount-immediately framing clearly.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'we do have our no worries damage coverage. Which is our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' Covers the $2,000 and 'included in hourly rate' but does not explicitly mention 'no deductible / no fine print' framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep never asked a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' after covering the Two Promises. The call moved directly from pricing into availability slots without closing out the promises section.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine version. The only concern check was at the very top of the call ('do you have any questions or concerns'), which the customer declined. No final check was conducted.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asked: 'Would you like us to help you with your move on Friday? October 2nd.' — plainly stated with no built-in out. Customer did not commit; instead said 'I'll go over this... I'll call back definitely if I want to go through it.' Rep accepted and offered to email details.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep did not mention rate lock or that the quote is guaranteed/locked. This was not addressed.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirmed arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM or 1:30–3:30 PM options offered), phone number (already had it), and addresses (origin and destination confirmed). Rep did NOT confirm the specific chosen date/time (customer did not commit), crew size (assumed 2 movers but not re-confirmed in booking context), or notes for the crew about concerns. Partial confirmation of what was discussed, but no actual booking lock since customer did not say yes.

top_strength: Brianne gathered comprehensive logistics details and special considerations early, painting a clear picture of the move (apartment-to-apartment, minimal load, elevator access question, fragile items) that allowed her to give a well-personalized estimate range without unnecessary back-and-forth.
coaching_note: The call stalled at the ask: deliver the quid pro quo framing in Section 1 before probing, ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate, run a genuine final concerns check in Section 6, and hold for a yes/commit before ending the call—right now the customer walked away with an email and no booking locked in.
booking_note: Customer said 'I'll kind of go over this and then...I'll call back definitely if I want to go through it' - no date/time was locked in, customer explicitly deferred decision to a future callback.
